steps.say: The Earth spins round once every 24 hours.
The side facing the Sun has day. The side facing away has night.

figure.alt: The Sun lighting up one side of the Earth.

steps.say: The Sun seems to move across the sky. Really, the Earth is spinning.
steps.show: The Sun rises in the east and sets in the west.

steps.say: Shadows are long in the morning and evening. They are short at midday.
Some animals are nocturnal. Owls and bats are active at night.

figure.alt: An owl and a bat, which are active at night.

check.prompt: Why do we have day and night?

options.text: The Sun moves around the Earth.
options.why: The Sun only seems to move. The Earth spins.
Night comes even when there are no clouds.

hints: Something turns our side towards and away from it.
Ask: which one spins, the Earth or the Sun?
check.explanation: The Earth spins. Our side faces the Sun for day and turns away for night.

check.prompt: How many hours does the Earth take to spin round once?
hints: One spin gives one day and one night.
Think about how many hours are in a whole day.
A clock goes round twice in a day: 12 hours each time.
check.explanation: The Earth takes about 24 hours to spin round once. That is one day and one night.
